newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures rise sharply on Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures rise sharply on Chicago.

text.p: Grains futures continued their week-long surge on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday with all eyes on trends in Chicago, traders said.
"The rise was certainly not due to domestic fundamentals as those would not have affected old crop prices," said Janos Szolyka of Swap.
Untraded maize rose by the daily 400 forint limit for all positions except March and May 1998.
October and December milling wheat accounted for the lion's share of turnover with 785 contracts out of a meagre grains total of 918.
Milling wheat attracted trade as prices were freed from the daily limit, Szolyka said.
"Nobody was prepared to sell at limit-up prices as they expect the rising trend to continue," he said.
October milling wheat rose 800 forints per tonne to 26,800 forints and December finished at 27,810, up 810.
Surging milling wheat prices triggered similar movements in other grains, resulting in August rising to 24,500 forints.
"This was clearly hysteria as feed wheat just is not worth as much as milling wheat," Szolyka said. The only traded feed wheat maturity was December, which rose 5,180 forints to 26,980.
Szolyka added that speculation over European Union export strategy might have contributed to the general rise.
July feed barley, the only position traded, gained 2,200 forints.
